3 Methodology
In this section, we describe in detail the workflow of 
our systematic review following the guideline by Keele, 
Staffs [92]. We introduce research questions, search strat -
egy, and the inclusion and exclusion criteria for selecting 
the studies, followed by data gathering methods and data 
interpretation.
3.1 Research questions
In line with our object to review privacy-preserving in 
blockchain-based solutions in healthcare data sharing, we 
aim to answer three research questions (RQs): 
1. RQ1: How is blockchain technology applied to health -
care data sharing?
2. RQ2: Which privacy-preserving technologies are used 
in blockchain-based health data sharing solutions?
3. RQ3: To what extent privacy-preserving solutions based 
on blockchain are established in healthcare?
3.2 Searching strategy
We selected peer-reviewed papers published in English 
from 2008 to 2024 with the following keywords: privacy, 
healthcare, blockchain, and sharing. We searched from 
the following engines and digital libraries: IEEE Xplore 
Digital Library, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, ACM Digital 
Library, and Web of Science. The search terms and filters 
used in each digital library are enlisted in Appendix A.

decoded by Bob’s (another participant) private key. When 
a data requester applies for it, the proxy can transform the 
ciphertext of healthcare data into one that the requester can 
decode with their private key. This way, healthcare data 
can be shared without revealing individual privacy. With a 
combination of cloud computing and proxy re-encryption, 
blockchain-based healthcare data sharing solutions can 
solve the issue of storing and transferring large amounts of 
healthcare data.
2.4 Technology readiness levels
To evaluate the maturity of technologies in blockchain-
based healthcare data sharing, we adopt the Technology 
Readiness Levels (TRLs) framework [89] shown in Table 7.
Initially developed by NASA, TRLs provide a structured 
assessment tool widely adapted across industries to measure 
the readiness of technologies from conceptual stages to full 
commercial deployment [ 90]. According to the European 
Association of Research and Technology Organisations 
(EARTO), the TRL scale, shown in Table 7, is highly adapt-
able, reflecting its broad application from space explora -
tion to healthcare innovations [ 91]. However, EARTO also 
highlights the need for adaptations to address specific sector 
challenges and the non-linear nature of innovation in con -
temporary R&D environments. This adaptability is essential 
in our study as it allows us to assess and categorize the tech-
nologies under review accurately, ensuring that stakehold -
ers can clearly understand the readiness of each technology 
for implementation in real-world settings.

resposta.resumo: O artigo descreve a metodologia de uma revisão sistemática sobre privacidade em compartilhamento de dados de saúde baseado em blockchain, apresentando três perguntas de pesquisa, estratégia de busca (2008‑2024, IEEE, ACM, etc.) e critérios de inclusão. Destaca o uso de proxy re‑encryption para compartilhar dados sem expor privacidade e adota os Níveis de Maturidade Tecnológica (TRL) para avaliar a prontidão das soluções, indicando que a maioria está em estágio de prova de conceito (TRL3).

perfil.problema: patients’ limited control over their healthcare data
perfil.solucao: Blockchain technology promises enhanced data ownership, control, and interoperability
perfil.avaliacao: most solutions remain at the proof-of-concept stage (TRL3)
perfil.limites: privacy-preserving search and verification remain underexplored
perfil.possibilidades: • Avaliar a integração de proxy re‑encryption com computação de borda em IoT urbano para reduzir latência e custos de contratos inteligentes. • Construir um roadmap TRL‑orientado para adoção de SSI e credenciais verificáveis em serviços de saúde de cidades inteligentes. • Criar um benchmark comparativo de técnicas de privacidade (ABE, ZKP, PEKS) aplicadas a blockchains híbridas (on‑chain/off‑chain) em cenários inter‑organizacionais.

evidencias.afirmacao: Proxy re‑encryption enables healthcare data to be shared without revealing individual privacy.
evidencias.citacao: When a data requester applies for it, the proxy can transform the ciphertext of healthcare data into one that the requester can decode with their private key.

evidencias.afirmacao: The study classifies technology maturity using TRL levels, identifying most solutions at TRL3.
evidencias.citacao: First assessment of the feasibility of the concept and technologies with prototypes

resposta.interpretacao: A revisão sistemática reforça que, embora blockchain ofereça potencial para controle de dados de saúde, as soluções ainda são incipientes (TRL3) e carecem de mecanismos robustos de busca e verificação de privacidade; o uso de proxy re‑encryption surge como estratégia prática para proteger dados durante o compartilhamento.
resposta.duvidas: • Como escalar o proxy re‑encryption para ambientes de alta frequência de dados IoT? • Quais adaptações são necessárias nos TRLs para refletir requisitos de privacidade específicos de cidades inteligentes? • Existe avaliação empírica de custos de armazenamento off‑chain combinado com re‑encryption em larga escala?
